s17_dimension_ranking_defect.was: predictions were emitted per-dimension AND ranked to name the single most vulnerable dimension
s17_dimension_ranking_defect.result: top-1 dimension accuracy 0.080 against random 0.200 and always-guess-estimator 0.902 -- WORSE THAN RANDOM
s17_dimension_ranking_defect.defect: the per-dimension scores are raw values of DIFFERENT features on DIFFERENT scales (rel_se, kurtosis, within_between, serial_ac). Ranking them against each other to pick a top-1 compares incomparable quantities. The ranking method was invalid; the per-dimension discrimination it was built on was not.
s17_dimension_ranking_defect.not_fixed_here: calibrating the four scores onto a common scale would require fitting on the evaluation population, which is the prohibited move. A corrected ranking needs its own dev/freeze/eval cycle.
s17_dimension_ranking_defect.status: the per-dimension result STANDS and replicates; the DIMENSION IDENTIFICATION claim is withdrawn

s17_design_revisions_on_dev.revision_1: fragility threshold gained an absolute floor, max(0.20, 0.5*|d_base|). Under the purely relative rule the dev base rate was 0.983 because any null-effect claim is fragile by construction.
s17_design_revisions_on_dev.revision_2: the noise perturbation was raised from 0.02 to 0.25 of the pooled sd after firing on 0 of 120 dev claims.
s17_design_revisions_on_dev.legitimacy: both were made on the DEVELOPMENT population, before the predictor was frozen and hashed, and are disclosed rather than absorbed. Nothing was changed after the freeze.

s17_unit_direction_narrative_error.verdict: ARCHAEON IS RIGHT. The frozen rule and my narrative point in OPPOSITE directions on the unit dimension.
s17_unit_direction_narrative_error.frozen_rule: unit <- serial_ac, higher_is_fragile = FALSE (raw dev AUC 0.13)
s17_unit_direction_narrative_error.my_narrative: 'serial dependence inside a world is exactly what makes observation-level pooling wrong, and it now predicts that failure' -- which asserts HIGHER serial_ac => MORE unit-fragile
s17_unit_direction_narrative_error.which_is_correct: THE FROZEN RULE. It is empirical and it replicated out of sample at 0.845 / 0.807 / 0.800 across three fresh populations. The narrative was a mechanistic story invented after the fact and it is wrong.
s17_unit_direction_narrative_error.mechanism_verified: the unit perturbation re-estimates by pooling all observations instead of world means, so the POOLED SD is what moves. High serial_ac means observations inside a world are near-copies, the pooled SD stays close to the between-world SD, and the estimate barely moves -- STABLE. Low serial_ac means large within-world variance, pooling inflates the denominator, and the estimate shifts -- FRAGILE. Measured: serial organism serial_ac 0.47 -> |delta| 0.14 not fragile; gaussian serial_ac -0.09 -> |delta| 1.46 fragile.
s17_unit_direction_narrative_error.root_cause: I conflated INFERENCE VALIDITY with ESTIMATE STABILITY. High serial dependence makes pseudo-replication MORE inferentially wrong, because n is inflated further, while making the point estimate MORE stable. Two different quantities moving in opposite directions. S10 drew exactly this distinction and I lost it in the S17 write-up.
s17_unit_direction_narrative_error.artifact_status: FROZEN ARTIFACT UNCHANGED. Only the narrative is corrected. selection_policy.json already carried the correct direction, so nothing Archaeon consumes was wrong -- the error was confined to my prose.
s17_unit_direction_narrative_error.scope_check: verified all five dimensions: ledger and shipped policy agree on feature and direction for estimator, transform, horizon and unit. noise has no rule in either.
